sentences.text: Germanodactylus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Upper Jurassic of Germany, including the Solnhofen Limestone.

A distinctive head crest is a key feature of the animal, and the soft-tissue component of this crest was first described in 2002 by S. Christopher Bennett. This soft-tissue portion was probably composed of cornified epidermis, making Germanodactylus the first genus known to have such a structure, though similar features were likely widespread among pterosaurs.
It has a nasoantorbital fenestra twice as long as the eye orbit.

G. cristatus has no teeth at the jaw tip and fewer teeth than G. rhamphastinus, which has approximately sixteen upper and fifteen lower teeth per side. The beak was long and narrow with few or no teeth; the teeth were short and peg-like, but absent at the tip, which instead had a horny extension. G. cristatus differs from G. rhamphastinus by not having teeth at the tip of the jaw. It has fewer teeth, thirteen on each side of the upper jaw and twelve on the lower compared to sixteen upper and fifteen lower on each side for G. rhamphastinus.
G. cristatus had a 0.98-meter wingspan and a 13-centimeter skull, while G. rhamphastinus had a 1.08-meter wingspan and a 21-centimeter skull.
A tentatively referred hindlimb suggests that G. cristatus may have reached sizes larger than the known specimens.

The first fossils, impressions of the animal in limestone, were discovered in 1892. The type species G. cristatus is based on specimen BSP 1892.IV.1 found in the Solnhofen limestone of Eichstätt, Germany. The type specimen for G. cristatus is BSP 1892.IV.1 from the Solnhofen limestone of Eichstätt, Germany. It was originally described by Plieninger in 1901 as a specimen of Pterodactylus kochi. Carl Wiman gave it its current species name in 1925, which means "crested" in Latin. Yang Zhongjian determined it deserved its own genus in 1964.

The species G. rhamphastinus was originally described by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1851 as a species of the genus Ornithocephalus. The species G. rhamphastinus is based on specimen BSP AS.I.745, a skeleton from the Mörnsheimer Limestone of Daiting, Germany. Peter Wellnhofer included G. rhamphastinus in the genus Germanodactylus in 1970.

G. cristatus has no teeth at the jaw tip and fewer teeth than G. rhamphastinus, which has approximately sixteen upper and fifteen lower teeth per side. The beak was long and narrow with few or no teeth; the teeth were short and peg-like, but absent at the tip, which instead had a horny extension.

Yang Zhongjian established the family Germanodactylidae for the genus. Bennett placed the genus in the family Pterodactylidae, while Alexander W.A. Kellner found it related to Pterodactylus in his 2003 analysis. In 2017, Vidovic and Martill created the new genus Altmuehlopterus for G. rhamphastinus. Its parent group is Lophocratia. It is classified in the class Reptilia. The type species is Germanodactylus cristatus.

Germanodactylus lived in what is now Germany during the Upper Jurassic and was discovered in Solnhofen Limestone rocks. It lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.

It is debated whether G. rhamphastinus deserves its own genus, "Daitingopterus", as suggested by Maisch and coauthors. Bennett suggested in 1996 that Germanodactylus represented adults of Pterodactylus, but this hypothesis was later rejected by further studies.
